name: AI Environment Swap Explainer
description: Reverse-engineered from a Reel by @quantumfloww_media. One talking-head take, with the background replaced by a new AI-generated environment on every sentence boundary. Captions run as 2-3 word chunks over the speaker's chest. The speaker never changes; only the world around them does.
visual_style: photoreal AI-composited environments, clean product-film lighting, soft neutral base grade, one continuous performance
environment: a new generated setting per sentence: dotted white studio, poster-lined walkway, corridor of screens, dark showroom, bright open-plan office, retail floor, long dark table, isometric colour-blocked space
caption_style: bold white sans-serif, tight black rounded box, 2-3 words per chunk, one chunk per ~1.2s, no emoji, no colour highlight
typography: heavy grotesk, tight tracking, sentence case
color_grading: neutral, low saturation on the speaker, saturation carried by the environment
music_description: quiet ambient pad that never competes with the voice; no drop, no build

name: Tutorial Multi-Mode Cepat
description: Opens on a large text hook, then keeps cycling visual modes — facecam, live demonstration, screen recording, output example — and closes on a comment-CTA card. Attention is held by changing what kind of thing you are looking at, not by cutting faster.
visual_style: screen-recording and facecam intercut with generated output, bright and utilitarian, no cinematic grade
environment: desk setup and application UI; the tool being taught stays on screen
caption_style: oversized hook text on the opening beat, then short white or yellow instruction captions carrying each step
typography: heavy sans, high contrast against the UI behind it

name: Presenter Split-Layout Stabil
description: The presenter holds a fixed bottom panel as the anchor while the top panel carries the demo, UI or output. The frame never rearranges, so the viewer never has to re-orient — the top panel changing is the only edit.
visual_style: fixed two-panel composition, presenter below and material above, even lighting, no cinematic grade
environment: presenter at a desk; the upper panel shows whatever is being explained
caption_style: short captions and labels sitting on the upper panel, close to what they describe
typography: clean sans, label weight rather than headline weight

name: Showcase Visual + Workflow
description: Leads with the finished visual to earn attention, drops into the process or UI as proof it is real, then returns to the visual as payoff. Result first, receipts second, result again.
visual_style: cinematic generated output alternating with plain workflow UI, the contrast between the two is the point
environment: generated scenes for the hook and payoff; application UI for the middle proof section
caption_style: short hook line up front, then proof labels naming the tool or step
typography: bold sans for the hook, lighter weight for proof labels

name: Cinematic-Led Sequence
description: A run of generated cinematic shots carries the whole narrative. No presenter, no UI — the footage is the argument. Built to sell output quality the way a trailer does.
visual_style: photoreal generated cinematography, consistent grade across every shot, feature-film framing
environment: continuous generated world; shots read as one location and one hour of day
caption_style: minimal — a brand mark or a single closing line, nothing competing with the frame
color_grading: warm cinematic grade held identical across shots
music_description: score carries the pacing since there is no dialogue to cut against

name: Alternating Cinematic Explainer
description: Alternates full-frame cinematic blocks with full-frame presenter blocks — B-roll, host, B-roll, host. Gets the pull of generated footage and the trust of a face without ever splitting the frame.
visual_style: full-frame cinematic generation alternating with full-frame talking head, each mode given the whole screen
environment: generated scenes for the B-roll blocks; a real room for the host blocks
music_styles: instrumental bed that ducks under the host
caption_style: sparse captions, with an occasional app logo when a tool is named
typography: minimal, used only where a name must be readable

name: Static Comparison Board
description: Reference and result sit on screen together in a layout that never moves, with almost no cuts. The comparison itself is the content — no process, no narration structure to follow.
visual_style: fixed comparison board, input and output side by side, flat and evenly lit
environment: no scene — the board is the frame
caption_style: one short explanatory line above the comparison, held for the whole shot
